scope.included: Base/core multiplayer game for 2–5 players; every material gameplay claim and important rules omission in the candidate, including quantities, sequencing, destinations, permissions, all five factions, all six structure bonus tile diagrams, immediate ending and scoring.
excluded: optional variants including Delay of Game
editorial metadata and nonmechanical introductory descriptions
scope.method: Fresh independent source-only comparison. Read the complete 32-page extracted rulebook, checked the candidate throughout, and visually inspected source PDF diagrams for production, player-mat benefits/recruits, structure tiles and final scoring. No candidate edits.
scope.independence: Did not read question banks, keys, reader outputs, grades, coverage materials, prior audit reports or parent history; did not author repairs.

checked_claims.claims: Clockwise individual turns without rounds; sixth star ends play immediately; final fortune rather than ending the game determines victory.
Each faction has one character, four mechs, eight workers, four structures, four recruits, six technology cubes and six stars; characters/mechs participate in combat; wooden components do not.
Shuffle relevant decks; select players plus one Factory cards without inspecting returned cards; random face-up structure tile; eleven encounter spaces; resources, coins and multipliers supplied.

Random faction/player mats, stated faction seating order, correct starting tracks/cards/coins by mat, character and two workers positioned correctly, remaining pieces correctly placed, recruit spaces empty, lowest numbered mat starts; objective/card contents secret, card count public, coin total need not be disclosed, combat card commitment may be concealed.

Different section, optional top followed by optional bottom, each once, either/both/neither permitted; full exposed red cost before optional green benefits; top gains can fund bottom cost; overlap turns during noninteractive bottom decisions; Rusviet repeat exception.

Home bases excluded from territories and normal movement/build/deploy destinations; expansion placeholders; unit/structure control and enemy worker displacement of structure control; defender retains temporary control pending combat; building abilities remain with owner, with Mill control exception.

Only four resource types; workers excluded; resources persist on board, can be spent from any controlled territories and return to supply; unlimited resource supply via multipliers; no friendly stacking limit.

Two different units one adjacent territory, or one coin before upgrades; sequential unit movement; all units carry resources; only mechs carry workers; carried workers retain their own movement eligibility; Speed adds a step for characters/mechs and permits intermediate loading/unloading.

Default river/lake restrictions and shoreline interpretation; printed tunnel adjacency; Mine personal tunnel even under enemy control; structures alone do not obstruct entry; worker movement restrictions; entering enemy units stops the character/mech; undefended workers retreat immediately with one popularity loss each, even if insufficient popularity, without combat.

Complete movement, resolve attacker-ordered combats before subsequent bottom action, then encounter/Factory as applicable; character encounter stop lasts the turn; lost contested encounter leaves token.

One coin for two power or one card; reshuffle combat discards as needed, no draw when exhausted; one coin for any two resources or one popularity; traded resources share a controlled worker territory; no resource Trade with all workers at home; Monument popularity and Armory power bonuses correctly assigned.

Pay all previously exposed costs before production; up to two distinct controlled territories before upgrades; one matching output per worker; mountain metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, village worker, lake/Factory none; outputs remain on producing territory; workers taken left to right after payment, optional, never returned to mat; newly exposed costs affect later actions; dead-turn procedure.
Additional production territory, Mill produces as a worker even without an actual worker, actual workers there also produce, requires owner control.

Oil/metal/wood/food costs correctly mapped; mat-dependent full costs and coins; paid completed actions still give coins/recruit bonuses; Upgrade cube moves from any green box to an empty bracketed red box, never solid-black-bordered red box.

Normal placement requires controlled worker territory; no lake deployment/building or home-base building; deployment unlocks ability for all mechs and character, not workers; Factory building allowed; one structure total per territory; structures permanent and opponent cannot use their abilities; four structure effects correctly assigned.

Any recruit to any empty one-time space, permanent; two power/coins/popularity/cards; ongoing bonus follows original bottom section; Upgrade power, Deploy coin, Build popularity, Enlist card, each one; own and adjacent players' matching bottom actions trigger; announcement required; active-left-right resolution; two-player opponent counted once; top/Factory/encounter exclusions; sixth-star priority.

Rusviet repeats including Factory; Crimea once-per-turn one-card/one-resource substitution irrespective of value; Nordic worker river crossing only; Polania up to two different encounter options in either order and first gain can pay second; Saxony unlimited available combat/objective stars and retains second objective.
Saxony/Nordic forests and mountains, Rusviet farms and villages, Crimea farms and tundra, Polania villages and mountains; unlocked character/mech scope and universal Speed correctly stated.
Underpass controlled mountains/tunnels/Mine adjacency for character/mechs; Disarm two opponent track power before tunnel/Mine combat once per combat.
Township controlled villages/Factory adjacency; People's Army adds one card total when any worker present and still requires character/mech, including correct example.
Seaworthy lake movement and adjacent-lake retreat including transported workers; Artillery pay one power to force two opponent power loss once per combat.
Wayfare to own/inactive bases including unused expansion bases regardless of distance, not active opponents; Scout steals one random combat card before combat once per combat.

checked_claims.topic: Polania mech abilities and lake restrictions
checked_claims.claims: Submerge lake movement and lake-to-lake adjacency; Camaraderie only after winning combat as aggressor on own turn, not undefended worker displacement; transported workers/resources cannot be abandoned on lakes, workers need mech to leave; lake combat possible; no Polania adjacent-lake retreat exception.

Zero power/popularity attacks allowed; attacker uses combat ability first; secret simultaneous dial zero through min(seven,current power), optional one card per character/mech plus Rusviet worker bonus; simultaneous reveal, attacker ties; both sides deduct dial and discard cards, card values do not cost track power.

Winner territory/resources and eligible mandatory star; ordinary two combat-star cap and Saxony exception; loser all units to home leaving resources, Nordic eligible retreat exception; attacker worker popularity penalty including lake-carried workers, defender no penalty; loser draws one card only after revealing positive power via dial/cards; unresolved later combat undone after sixth star.

Character only, after movement/all combats; token discarded on resolution; card shown and thematic capitals read aloud; required affordable option except Polania ability; full printed cost and optional benefits; all gained units/resources/structures at encounter location; no normal action costs or other mat/recruit bonuses; card face-down under deck.

Each character's first finished Move there must select a card; one permanent card per player, no exchange; fifth section optional top then bottom and normal repeat rule; no analogous mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses; bottom Move one unit up to two steps, three for Speed character/mech, with Mine and normal stops.

Reveal completed objective only own turn before/after top/bottom, may wait but all requirements at reveal; normal one star and both cards under deck, Saxony retains other; only coins tangible exchanges, unenforceable agreements, tournament coin-deal prohibition; cannot negotiate away initiated combat.

Six upgrades, four mechs/buildings/recruits, eight workers, objective, combat, eighteen popularity, sixteen power; ordinary once per category except two combats; stars permanent/unblocked by others; sixth immediately ends with no equalizing turn; bottom primary benefit/coins/own recruit benefit completed before star; neighbor bonuses active-left-right and no later resolution after ending; pending mixed movement undone.

checked_claims.claims: Unique adjacent printed tunnels: 1/2–3/4–5/6 pay 2/4/6/9; unique adjacent lakes and encounters: 1/2–3/4–5/6–7 pay 2/4/6/9; structures on printed tunnels: 1/2/3–4 pay 2/4/6; longest continuous straight structure row and combined farm/tundra structures: 1/2/3/4 pay 2/4/6/9; Mine excluded as tunnel feature, removed encounter tokens still count, rivers do not break adjacency/row, each adjacent feature once, enemy control does not remove bonus, zero features gives zero.

limitations: Verdict is confined to the supplied 2016 core rulebook and the stated multiplayer scope; no external FAQ, later revision, component-card corpus or benchmark material was consulted.

The summary intentionally directs players to their physical Player Mat for exact mat-dependent costs, coin values and upgraded exposed benefits; reproducing every Player Mat is not required for this summary.

Optional teaching/scoring demonstrations, combat-card frequency distribution, narrative character histories, full global component inventory and source metadata are not material omissions for this gameplay summary.
conclusion: No material contradiction or important core multiplayer rules omission found. Candidate is consistent with the complete supplied rulebook and the visually checked production, recruit, six-tile and scoring diagrams.
